name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,321

entries.clue: Staff close to chimney stacks (4)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its end, so this takes the final letter

blocks.note: to staff a post is to man it

annotation.surface: Tall chimney stacks rising beside a factory's workforce.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stacks' looks like a noun belonging to the chimney, but it is the definition: stacks of money means many, a colloquial quantity.
annotation.definitionFit: A colloquial sense: having stacks of something means having a great quantity, a determiner-like use matching many.

entries.clue: Worried about final courses (8)

indicatorNotes.about: turning about means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

annotation.surface: A student anxious about the last classes of their degree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Courses' suggests study, but it is the meal sense: the sweet course comes last. STRESSED and DESSERTS are a famous mirror pair.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the dining sense: puddings are the courses served at the close of a meal.

entries.clue: Choir members wanting introduction to Robert Burns (6)

indicatorNotes.wanting: wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken away
indicatorNotes.introduction to: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the people who make up a choir
first letter of Robert, removed from the choir members

annotation.surface: A choir struggling to begin a song by Robert Burns, the Scottish poet.
annotation.walkthrough: Robert Burns reads as one name, the national poet of Scotland; the clue splits him, with Robert feeding the wordplay and 'Burns' as a verb being the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to scorch the surface of something is to burn it lightly.

entries.clue: Concerning schoolgirl lacking in care (6)

blocks.note: re = concerning, as in a memo heading
a miss is a young girl

annotation.surface: A report worrying about a pupil who is neglected.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Concerning' looks like an adjective meaning worrying, but it is the preposition 'about', which crosswords shorten to RE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: negligent, falling short of the attention one ought to give.

entries.clue: Minister belonging to correct organisation (6)

indicatorNotes.belonging to: the answer belongs to, sits inside, the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the second letter of the first word into the start of the second

annotation.surface: A clergyman who belongs to the proper church body.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface already sounds ecclesiastical, which hides the fact that the answer is spelt out across 'correct organisation'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a parish priest in the Church of England is one kind of minister of religion.

entries.clue: Server used by revolutionary multimedia magazine (4)

indicatorNotes.used by: the letters are used by, taken from within, the phrase that follows
indicatorNotes.revolutionary: a revolution turns something round, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the last three letters of the first word plus the first of the second

annotation.surface: A radical multimedia magazine running on a computer server.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Server' looks like computing, matching multimedia, but it is someone who serves in a household.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a domestic servant is one who serves.

entries.clue: Pedant — one determined to hold line (8)

indicatorNotes.to hold: one piece holds the other inside it

blocks.note: a sticker is one who sticks at things, determined

annotation.surface: A pedant is someone resolved to stick to the party line.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface nearly defines the answer twice over, so solvers may hunt for a single-word synonym; the dash separates the definition from the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who insists on exactness in small matters.

entries.clue: Part of court policy introduced by HQ (8)

indicatorNotes.introduced by: the second piece is introduced by, so comes after, the first

blocks.note: the party line is its policy

annotation.surface: A new rule for part of the law courts brought in by head office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the back line at each end of a tennis court is one part of it.

entries.clue: Judge commander-in-chief hosting short ceremony (6)

indicatorNotes.hosting: a host has a guest inside, so one piece contains the other
indicatorNotes.short: short means cut, so the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A judge and a supreme commander hosting a brief formal ceremony.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Judge' reads as a courtroom figure; here it is anyone who passes judgement on work.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a reviewer judges the merits of books, plays or food.

entries.clue: Faculty certainly entertained by boat crew (8)

indicatorNotes.entertained by: a guest is entertained inside a host, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a rowing eight is a boat crew of eight oarsmen

annotation.surface: University staff agreeing to be hosted by the rowing team.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Faculty' suggests a university department; it is a faculty in the sense of a bodily sense or power.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: sight is one of the faculties, the natural powers of the body.

entries.clue: Sound made by animal’s fur (4)

indicatorNotes.Sound made by: the answer is the sound of the word that follows

annotation.surface: Asking what noise a furry creature makes.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks for an animal's noise, but 'sound' here means a word that sounds the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an animal's coat is the growth covering its skin.

entries.clue: One of man’s best friends publicised trouble on the radio (8)

indicatorNotes.on the radio: radio is heard, not seen, so the word goes by its sound

blocks.note: to air views is to publicise them

annotation.surface: A dog's problem made public in a radio broadcast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man's best friend' is the stock phrase for a dog; the answer is a large terrier breed.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the stock phrase means a dog, and this terrier is one breed.

entries.clue: Learner driver overwhelmed by unfamiliar throttle (8)

indicatorNotes.overwhelmed by: to be overwhelmed is to be engulfed, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: L, from the L-plate a learner driver displays

annotation.surface: A nervous learner swamped by an unfamiliar car's accelerator.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Throttle' sits beside driver and reads as a car's accelerator; it is the verb, to choke.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to choke someone by squeezing the throat.

entries.clue: Article writer abandoning subject (3)

indicatorNotes.abandoning: one piece abandons, leaves out, the other

blocks.note: a setter writing of their own role uses ME

annotation.surface: A journalist dropping the topic of a piece.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article.
annotation.definitionFit: A grammatical term: the definite article is one of English's articles.

entries.clue: Seeing how marzipan on cake might be described? (8)

annotation.definition2: how marzipan on cake might be described?

blocks.clueFragment: how marzipan on cake might be described?
blocks.note: marzipan is the layer under the frosting, so a description of what it is not

annotation.surface: Observing a baker describe a marzipan-topped cake.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: split the answer as NOT ICING and it describes the marzipan layer. The question mark flags the play.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a plain synonym for observing, and a whimsical split, NOT ICING, for a layer of marzipan.

entries.clue: Main’s current share is distributed (5,3)

indicatorNotes.distributed: letters that are distributed are spread around into a new order

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: A mains electricity supply, its share of power spread out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Main' reads as mains power, helped by 'current', but it is the old poetic word for the open sea.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example using an old poetic sense: the main is the open sea, and this is one sea.

entries.clue: Protective device is held in an unusual way (6)

indicatorNotes.in an unusual way: the letters are arranged unusually, into a new order

annotation.surface: A safety gadget that is gripped awkwardly.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a description of how the device is carried, which neatly disguises that 'is held' is the raw material.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a plate carried to ward off blows is one kind of protective device.

entries.clue: Sailor reportedly managed to avoid capture (6)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is heard, so the word goes by its sound

blocks.note: to duck something is to avoid it

annotation.surface: A news report of a sailor who evaded being taken prisoner.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has the sailor escaping capture, the opposite of the answer; 'capture' is the definition, as a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym as verbs: to seize a person and carry them off by force.

entries.clue: Rent until end of October/beginning of November (4)

indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its final letter
indicatorNotes.beginning of: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: as in nine to five: until five

annotation.surface: A lease on a flat running until the turn of October into November.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a payment for housing, but it is the past participle of rend.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rent is the past participle of rend, to rip apart.

entries.clue: Excellent penalty (4)

blocks.note: a sum of money paid as punishment

annotation.surface: Praise for a well-taken penalty kick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Penalty' tempts a football reading, but it is the monetary kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adjective for high quality, and a noun for a monetary punishment.

entries.clue: Show I acted in gets recast (8)

indicatorNotes.gets recast: the letters are recast, set in a new mould

annotation.surface: An actor whose play is being given a new cast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Show' and 'recast' both speak of theatre, but 'Show' is the verb, to point out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to point something out or make it evident.

entries.clue: Bad-tempered, failing to complete series of questions (4)

indicatorNotes.failing to complete: the word is not completed, so it loses its last letter

blocks.note: irritable, with its final letter dropped

annotation.surface: A cross student who cannot finish an exam.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures an exam paper left unfinished; in fact it is the word for bad-tempered that is left incomplete.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: an exam is a set of questions put to examine someone.

entries.clue: Indigenous tribe’s first to stop displaying credulity (6)

indicatorNotes.first: the first letter of the word before
indicatorNotes.to stop: a stopper plugs a gap, so the letter goes inside

annotation.surface: A tribe that is the first to stop being gullible.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First' reads as 'the earliest', but here it takes the opening letter of 'tribe'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: belonging to a place by birth or origin.

entries.clue: Chapter in lesson about monster’s home? (4,4)

indicatorNotes.in: one piece goes in the other
indicatorNotes.about: knocked about, the letters change order

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation for chapter, as in 'ch. 3'

annotation.surface: A book chapter within a lesson about a monster's lair.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a hint rather than a synonym: the answer is a lake in the Scottish Highlands.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by allusion: the lake is famous as the supposed home of Nessie, the legendary monster.

entries.clue: Champion’s very good goal (6)

blocks.note: an end is an aim or goal

annotation.surface: A football champion scoring a superb goal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Champion' looks like a winner, a noun; it is the verb, as in championing a cause.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to champion a cause is to stand up for it.
